en: Mayon Volcano in Albay is famous for having a nearly perfect conical shape.
The Philippine eagle is a critically endangered bird of prey endemic to the forests of the Philippines.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching approximately 505 kilometers through the Cagayan Valley.
The freshwater fish sardinella tawilis is found exclusively in Taal Lake, making it the only marine sardine living in a freshwater lake.
Mount Apo in Davao is the highest mountain in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 cone-shaped hills that turn brown during the dry season.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a UNESCO World Heritage site protecting diverse coral reefs.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park in Palawan features an eight-kilometer navigable underground river flowing directly into the sea.
The Philippines experiences the habagat, a southwest monsoon that brings heavy rainfall to the western parts of the country during summer.
The Philippines holds the world's largest known deposit of nickel, primarily mined from laterite ore in Surigao and Palawan.
Palawan is the longest province in the Philippines, stretching over 400 kilometers between the South China Sea and the Sulu Sea.
The Rafflesia schadenbergiana, found in Mount Kitanglad, is the largest flower in the Philippines and can grow up to 80 centimeters wide.
